predecessors.name: Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic
predecessors.text: the territory of the Lithuanian SSR, which 'restored Lithuania's prewar name of the Republic of Lithuania'

predecessors.name: Lithuania, 1918-1940 (Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Lithuania' row)
predecessors.text: the interwar state, 'abolished by foreign forces in 1940', whose sovereign powers the Act of 11 March 1990 'is re-established'

ledger.x: 1990: the Supreme Council re-establishes an independent Lithuania on 11 March.
1991: Soviet forces storm the broadcasting centre in Vilnius on 13 January.
1991: the Soviet Union recognises Lithuania on 6 September.

wars.name: January Events
wars.outcome: Soviet forces seized the broadcasting buildings in Vilnius with 14 dead and about 700 injured; the Soviet Union nevertheless recognised Lithuania on 6 September 1991.

certainty.note: 1990-91 is the Lithuanian SSR's republic boundary; the border treaties with Latvia, Belarus and Russia (Kaliningrad) were not on the pages opened (unverified: page budget), but all are drawn as treaty lines.

sources.title: Act of the Re-Establishment of the State of Lithuania
